newsitem.title: CHINA: Southern China to set up big disc-producing base.
newsitem.headline: Southern China to set up big disc-producing base.

text.p: China will set up its biggest compact disc production base in the southern province of Guangdong as part of efforts to crack down on piracy, officials said on Monday.

The project would have the capacity to produce 40 million compact discs, video compact discs and CD-ROMs a year after it goes into operation, an official of the Guangdong Press and Publications Administration said in a telephone interview.
The annual output value of the base, with total investment of 80 million yuan ($9.6 million), would be 300-500 million yuan, the official said but declined to say when it would go into operation.
"The base will partly hit the pirate disc market," she said but gave no further details.
Customs in Jiangmen town in Guangdong seized 155,282 smuggled compact discs last April in China's biggest case involving imports of contraband compact discs, the China news service said.
Local Shantou customs nabbed 99,500 smuggled compact discs in May, including 79,500 pornographic discs, it said.

Last year's winter crackdown on piracy and pornography had snared nearly 1.9 million illegal VCDs and led to the closure of 40 illegal VCD production lines in southern Guangdong province, state media has said.
China should speed up construction of legal VCD production bases and develop the rental industry to push pirated goods out of the market, it said.

China and the United States went to the brink of a trade war in June last year over Washington's accusations that Beijing was not doing enough to combat rampant piracy of intellectual property rights.
